articles.title: How Ghunsa tragedy was turned into triumph
articles.summary: Twenty years after a helicopter crash in Ghunsa, Taplejung that claimed the lives of Nepal's leading conservationists, including Dr. Chandra Gurung, the community commemorates the tragedy by highlighting the lasting impact of their work. The memorial event honors their contributions to protecting the Himalaya's biodiversity and showcases how local forest management, community-based conservation projects, and eco‑tourism initiatives have flourished, turning a sorrowful loss into a catalyst for environmental stewardship. Officials, NGOs, and residents reflected on the progress made in wildlife protection, sustainable livelihoods, and the establishment of protected areas that were championed by the fallen experts, underscoring a narrative of resilience and hope.

articles.title: The Mary Slusser expose
articles.summary: The article examines the archives of American scholar Mary Slusser, revealing that her collections contain evidence of illicit removal of Nepalese cultural artifacts. While the archives document the extent of theft, they also provide detailed provenance information that could aid in the restitution of these items to Nepal. The piece highlights the paradox of scholarly work that both preserves and exposes wrongdoing, and discusses ongoing efforts by Nepalese authorities and international bodies to recover the stolen heritage.

articles.title: Turkish Airlines Named Europe's Best Airline
articles.summary: Turkish Airlines has been awarded the title of Best Airline in Europe for the 11th time at the Skytrax World Airline Awards 2026. The airline was recognized for its service quality, safety standards, and overall passenger experience, beating other major European carriers. The accolade highlights Turkish Airlines' continued focus on expanding its network and improving customer satisfaction, reinforcing its position as a leading carrier in the region.

articles.title: Nepal takes its message to the world
articles.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah will address the UN, highlighting the country's flood as a global warning.

articles.title: Nepal appoints non-political figures as ambassadors
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has appointed thirteen new ambassadors drawn from academic, economic, security and development sectors, as well as a senior military officer, rather than career politicians. The move signals a shift toward professional expertise in diplomatic postings, aiming to enhance Nepal's international representation and policy effectiveness.

articles.title: FUTURE SHOCKS
articles.summary: The recent Bhote Kosi‑Trisuli flood underscored the vulnerability of riverside towns across Nepal. The disaster caused significant damage and loss of life, prompting calls for improved flood‑risk management, early warning systems, and stronger infrastructure in vulnerable settlements. Experts say the event serves as a stark lesson for other communities situated along Nepal’s rivers, urging authorities to prioritize disaster preparedness and climate‑adaptation measures.

articles.title: Glacier melting is black and white
articles.summary: The article warns that rapid glacier melt in the Himalayas is a stark indicator of climate change, describing the phenomenon as both 'black and white' – a clear sign of environmental crisis. It argues that reducing air pollution, particularly black carbon emissions, is the most immediate and effective measure to protect the Himalayan icecap and slow glacier retreat. The piece emphasizes the urgency for Nepal and neighboring countries to adopt stricter pollution controls and invest in clean energy to safeguard water resources and ecosystems dependent on the glaciers.

articles.title: Death toll rises in Nepal flood
articles.summary: A severe flood in Nepal has caused the death toll to rise, with many casualties including children. At least 102 children have been left orphaned, highlighting the humanitarian crisis. Relief agencies are mobilizing to provide aid and support to the affected families.

articles.title: Climate warming set off Nepal disaster: Report
articles.summary: Scientists conclude global warming influenced catastrophic mountain collapse in Nepal.

articles.title: Even gods were not spared by the flood
articles.summary: Heavy rains caused a severe flood in Nepal's Trisuli Valley, a region revered for its sacred geography. The same natural features that made the valley a spiritual hub also rendered it highly vulnerable to the deluge, leading to damage of temples and cultural sites. Residents and authorities are grappling with the aftermath, assessing the impact on both the local community and the region's religious heritage.

articles.title: FlyDubai to PHH
articles.summary: FlyDubai will start direct flights from Pokhara to Dubai on 23 September, potentially boosting tourism in the city.

articles.title: Power import
articles.summary: India has increased its daily electricity export to Nepal, supplying up to 654 MW for 18 hours each day to help meet Nepal's energy needs after recent shortages. The boost aims to stabilize Nepal's power grid and support its recovery from the recent energy shortfall.

articles.title: Prithvi Highway
articles.summary: The Prithvi Highway, a main highway artery to Kathmandu, has been reopened after being blocked by landslides for nearly 18 days.

articles.title: Tiger sanctuary
articles.summary: The Nepalese government plans to establish a 50‑hectare tiger sanctuary in Devnagar, located in the buffer zone of Chitwan National Park. The sanctuary will provide a natural habitat for problem tigers that have come into conflict with humans, aiming to reduce human‑wildlife clashes while preserving the species. The initiative reflects ongoing conservation efforts to protect Nepal’s tiger population and manage wildlife‑human interactions more sustainably.

articles.title: EV registration
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has resumed the registration process for public electric vehicles after a four‑month suspension. The move aims to facilitate the entry of electric buses and other public transport into the market, supporting the country's green mobility goals. Officials indicated that the pause was due to administrative and technical adjustments, and the reopening will allow operators to complete necessary paperwork and obtain registration plates for their electric fleets.

articles.title: Maternity Bill
articles.summary: The Ministry for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs in Nepal has drafted an amendment to the Safe Motherhood and Reproductive Health Rights Act of 2018. The proposed changes aim to strengthen legal protections for pregnant women and new mothers, potentially expanding maternity leave, improving workplace accommodations, and enhancing access to reproductive health services. The draft will be presented to Parliament for discussion and approval, signaling the government's continued focus on women's health and gender equity.

articles.title: Ambassador list
articles.summary: The Nepalese Ministry of Foreign Affairs has completed its shortlist of candidates for ambassadorial posts, covering 21 of the 22 vacant diplomatic missions. The list, which will be presented for final approval, aims to fill key overseas postings and strengthen Nepal's diplomatic representation. The remaining vacancy and the selection process are expected to be addressed shortly.

articles.title: Pokhara calling
articles.summary: The Centara Collection’s Himalayan Hideaway Resort in Pokhara welcomed a delegation of Indian travel and media professionals for a three‑night, four‑day familiarisation trip. The itinerary showcased Pokhara’s natural attractions, adventure activities, cultural sites, and the resort’s luxury amenities, aiming to boost inbound tourism from India. Participants were given guided tours, networking sessions with local tourism officials, and opportunities to experience local cuisine and crafts. The event highlights growing collaboration between Nepal’s hospitality sector and Indian travel operators to capture the post‑pandemic travel surge.

articles.title: Mustang conference
articles.summary: The two‑day Gharpajhong Climate Conference kicked off on Tuesday in Mustang, Nepal, attracting more than 2,000 participants, including representatives from 431 local governments. The event aims to discuss climate‑related challenges and solutions for the region, fostering collaboration among municipal leaders and stakeholders.

articles.title: Marriott relief
articles.summary: Aloft by Marriott, a hotel in Kathmandu's Thamel district, has donated Rs.1.5 million to the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund. The contribution reflects the hospitality brand’s support for national relief efforts following recent disasters, aligning corporate social responsibility with government initiatives.

articles.title: Nepali families who lost everything twice
articles.summary: The article recounts the plight of Nepali families from the Khalte area who survived the devastating 2015 earthquake only to lose everything again when the Trisuli River flooded years later. It highlights the compounded trauma, loss of homes and livelihoods, and the challenges faced in rebuilding amid recurring natural disasters, while calling attention to the need for stronger disaster preparedness and support for affected communities.

articles.title: Price war and flood cloud Nepal EV market
articles.summary: The article discusses how Nepal's electric vehicle (EV) market is caught between a price war among manufacturers and the challenges posed by seasonal flooding. While battery‑powered cars are becoming cheaper to purchase, the lack of reliable charging infrastructure and flood‑damaged roads and power supply make trips more uncertain and costly. The piece highlights the tension between lower upfront prices and higher operational expenses, suggesting that without improved infrastructure and flood mitigation, the growth of EV adoption in Nepal may stall.

articles.title: Nepal tallies the cost of its disaster
articles.summary: Nepal has estimated the economic cost of recovering from a recent disaster at $4.7 billion, with the majority of losses stemming from destroyed hydropower projects. The figure underscores the severe impact on the country’s energy infrastructure and highlights the financial challenges ahead for reconstruction and rehabilitation efforts.

articles.title: Rescue Nepal’s stolen artefacts from auctioneers
articles.summary: The article reports on recent efforts by Nepalese authorities and cultural heritage groups to halt the auction of artefacts that were illegally removed from the country. It highlights the importance of both documentation and collective cultural memory in establishing provenance, and describes legal and diplomatic steps taken to retrieve the items before they are sold to foreign collectors. The piece underscores the urgency of protecting Nepal’s historical treasures and calls for stronger international cooperation to prevent future looting.

articles.title: The survivors of Syaprubesi
articles.summary: The article recounts the plight of residents from Syaprubesi who have lost their homes and livelihoods, likely due to a natural disaster. Seeking safety and a fresh start, they have taken refuge in a monastery in Kathmandu, where they find support and renewed hope for rebuilding their lives.
